To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

adding aerobic exercise training in obese women with intra-abdominally obese phenotype is more effective in reducing intra-abdominal adipose tissue compared to diet alone, and the abdominal fat reduction is dependent on obesity phenotype.
adding aerobic exercise training (DE) to a diet-alone program (DA) for 14 weeks in overweight and obese women with IF obesity phenotype significantly increased abdominal fat reduction compared to DA.
abdominal fat loss in response to weight reduction was modified by obesity phenotype and by adding aerobic exercise training.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of adding aerobic exercise to a diet program on abdominal fat reduction and the modification of obesity phenotype on abdominal subcutaneous and visceral fat reduction in response weight loss.
the effects on abdominal adiposity reduction of adding aerobic training to a diet-only weight-loss program and obesity phenotype.
the effects on abdominal subcutaneous and visceral fat reductions of adding aerobic exercise to a diet-alone program and obesity phenotype (IF obesity and ASF obesity) in response to weight-loss.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of exercise training to a weight-reduction diet program is more effective for reducing intra-abdominal adipose tissue in women with IF obesity phenotype.
the efficacy of adding aerobic exercise to diet for reducing abdominal fat is more prominent (1.3 times greater) in subjects with IF compared to those with ASF obesity.
the IF reduction is greater for IF obese individuals and the ASF reduction is greater for ASF obese individuals in response to a weight-reduction intervention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for IF obesity phenotype, the efficacy of adding aerobic exercise on reducing IF in response to a weight-reduction diet is greater (1.3 times).
the abdominal fat reduction is greater for individuals with ASF obesity than for those with IF obesity, and the IF reduction is greater for subjects with IF obesity than for subjects with ASF.

for individuals with ASF obesity, a weight-reduction program with diet alone is more efficient than adding aerobic exercise training; whereas, for individuals with IF phenotype, adding aerobic exercise training is more effective than diet alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
exercise training can help to reduce intra-abdominal visceral fat and that this is particularly the case for individuals with a high intra-abdominal obesity phenotype.
abdominal fat reduction in overweight and obese women may be enhanced by adding aerobic exercise to a diet-alone program, especially for those with IF obesity.
the obesity phenotype is an important factor to consider in the design of weight-loss interventions, particularly when abdominal fat reduction is the main objective.
